textRuns.value: Recommendation: replace daily 1.96 peeking with a pre-registered O'Brien-Fleming plan, gate every readout on SRM, and report shrunk lifts.

- Peeking: on the real checkpoint schedules, stopping at the first |z| >= 1.96 has a ~19% false positive rate, not 5%. 20 of 99 primary arms cross 1.96 at some point and the full-horizon answer disagrees.
- OBF holds the error at ~5%, calls 24 of the 26 significant arms the same way, and stops a median 25 days early (median test length 44 days). That frees ~750 arm-days of traffic.
- mSPRT is always valid (~1% FPR) but only recovers 18 of 26. Use it for continuous monitoring and kill switches, not for the ship call.

- Trust: 9 arms (9%) fail SRM with shares like 49.2% on millions of users. That is a bug (assignment, logging, bot filtering), not noise. 3 more arms are far from 50/50 and need their planned split confirmed. Two arms also lost treatment users between checkpoints, and one experiment had an empty checkpoint.
- Portfolio: 14 SHIP, 10 STOP (primary harm), 63 inconclusive, 12 untrusted. 1 in 7 wins and 1 in 10 hurts. Short tests (<= 3 weeks) never shipped, and 15% of them were harmful.
- Winner's curse: true effects vary by ~0.7% between experiments. Precise wins barely move, noisy ones collapse (e.g. +1.9% -> +0.4%). Forecast with shrunk numbers.
- Metrics: final z-scores of the 4 metrics correlate 0.89-0.97. Keep M1 plus one guardrail and review the rare disagreements before dropping the others.
- Robustness: across alpha 0.01-0.10 and guardrail margins 0-3%, SHIP ranges from 6 to 17. Above a 1% margin the guardrails stop binding. The peeking and SRM findings do not depend on these settings.

Caveat: metrics are anonymised. Calling M1 primary and M2-M4 guardrails is this program's assumed policy, not ASOS's actual practice. Source: ASOS Digital Experiments Dataset (Liu et al. 2021), CC BY 4.0.
